solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Company's head has to block complete acquisition

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in the middle of it, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: complete as in 'complete nonsense' means pure

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firm's chief executive tries to stop a takeover from going through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complete' is an adjective meaning utter, as in 'pure nonsense'; 'to block' puts the head of Company's and 'has' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase is something bought, so the two words are synonyms for an item obtained.

clue.text: Secretary detaining official and politician as an opener

indicators.note: detaining means holding in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
a ref is a referee, a match official
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A secretary holds back an official and an MP before the meeting begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detaining' means the secretary holds the official inside; the politician is a Tory, a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefatory remarks introduce a book or speech, so they serve to open it.

clue.text: Regret group of soldiers succeeded, blocking another group

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way inside, so these letters go within the other

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army
OR, other ranks, means the soldiers who are not officers
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: An army unit's success is spoiled by another unit getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts ORS inside REME, the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the sorrow felt for a wrong one has done; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Initially had yen to avoid holidaying couple in Pacific islands

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter
to avoid means to keep out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: someone on holiday is away
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
II is the Roman numeral two, a couple

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a holiday but a couple skip the Pacific trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid yen' takes the Y out of AWAY, leaving AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state is a chain of islands in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Town's upset about new article that's manufactured

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround the others
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a city is a town, and 's adds the S
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A town is upset about a new factory-made item.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the word upside down, giving SYTIC; 'about' wraps that around the new article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something artificial, made by industrial processes rather than nature, is described this way.

clue.text: No holding boy in battle

indicators.note: holding means clasping something within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
Seb, short for Sebastian, is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A refusal that keeps a lad out of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Naseby (1645) was a decisive battle of the English Civil War, fought in Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an example: the clash at this English village in 1645 was a famous Civil War engagement.

clue.text: Nervy, with hint of tension inside? That's not marked

indicators.note: inside places this letter within the other word

parts.note: neural means relating to the nerves

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone jittery with a touch of stress wonders if it shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts T, the 'hint of tension', inside NEURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour of no distinct hue, or ground favouring no side, is unmarked by any strong character.

clue.text: Go easy on arranged deals — frequently pressure will be involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped inside, so these letters go within the rearranged ones
arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Negotiators tone down business deals that keep coming under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes SEDAL; 'will be involved' wraps it around 'frequently' and the pressure symbol, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano's soft pedal dampens the sound, so as a verb it means to play something down.

clue.text: Central American food — it's fed to donkey

indicators.note: fed to means put inside, as food goes into a mouth, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey in Spanish-speaking America

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish being given to a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' puts the word 'it' inside the donkey, here the Spanish-American word for a small donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled tortilla with a filling is a staple of Mexican cooking, so it is a regional dish.

clue.text: Fellow returning after leaving a wood

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter of 'a' comes out
returning means going back, so the word for fellow is read backwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man walks back out of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MALE into ELAM; 'leaving a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree gives a hard timber, so its name is a type of wood.

clue.text: One stands, taking position on board, prepared for any blow

definitions.text: One stands, taking position on board, prepared for any blow

parts.words: One stands, taking position on board, prepared for any blow
parts.note: someone standing on a sailboard waits for any gust of air to drive it along

explanation.surface: A person stands at the ready, braced for whatever punch comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' reads as a punch, but it is a gust of air; 'board' is the sailboard, not a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailboarders ride standing on a board and need breezes, so they welcome any gust.

clue.text: Song by a drunk affording no escape…

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy singer belts out a tune, and there is no getting away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed so that no air can get in or out leaves nothing a way to escape.

clue.text: …and that of salesman makes you go

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
that stands for the song of the previous clue, an air

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a salesman's song is so bad it drives you away.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clues: 'that' means the song, AIR, from the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is an old-fashioned way of saying to go there, as in retiring to the drawing room.

clue.text: Heading away from Channel port to the other side

indicators.note: the heading of the word is its first letter, which goes away

parts.note: Dover is the English port on the Channel facing France

explanation.surface: Steaming away from a port on the English Channel bound for France.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is England's main Channel ferry port; 'Heading away from' drops its first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing across something takes you from one side to the far side, as in going across the sea.

clue.text: Cathedral treasure rarely taken out: I question its contents

indicators.note: its contents means what goes inside, so these letters are put within the others
taken out suggests the letters are moved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cathedral's treasure is seldom brought out, and someone queries what is in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' makes RELARY; 'its contents' means 'I question' goes inside that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for holy relics kept in a church or cathedral is often a richly decorated treasure.

clue.text: Crosses back carrying board for part of farm building

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one word goes inside the other
back means going in the reverse direction, so the word for crosses is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, a cross
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone crosses back across the yard bearing a plank to the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' is a noun here, roods; 'back' gives SDOOR and 'carrying' wraps it around the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's stall in a farm building has its own entrance, so this is a component of that building.

clue.text: Say upset amongst pub staff is a means of moving forward

indicators.note: amongst places these letters among the others

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a staff is a pole

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say

explanation.surface: An upset among the bar workers is a way of making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub staff' is not bar workers but two words, pub and staff; 'upset' turns 'Say' around, and 'amongst' sets it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole is pushed against the riverbed to propel a canal boat along.

clue.text: Greyish-brown in colour, insect is unwanted

indicators.note: in places this word inside the colour

parts.note: red is a colour
dun is a dull greyish-brown
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A dull-coloured insect that nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in colour' means inside the colour; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made jobless is surplus to requirements, no longer needed.

clue.text: The Spanish engaged in cowardly playing leading to referee's sanction

indicators.note: engaged in means involved inside, so one set of letters goes within the other
playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A footballer's timid play earns a booking from the official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' makes YLOWCARD; 'engaged in' places the Spanish article inside it after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows this coloured caution to book a player for an offence.

clue.text: Broadcaster to turn resentful with British pulling out

indicators.note: pulling out means withdrawing, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to embitter someone is to make them resentful

explanation.surface: A radio presenter grows bitter when the British leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling out' removes B from EMBITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sends out signals or radiation transmits them, so it is a broadcasting device.

clue.text: Women and others recline, ignoring one fight

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to lie is to recline
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Women and others lie back, not wanting a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring one' removes I from LIE, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with an opponent is to fight hand to hand; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Either limit to land for nobleman

indicators.note: to here means set against, so the partner word goes between the two limits
the limits of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

parts.note: either...or go together, so either calls up its partner word

explanation.surface: A boundary on each side of an estate belongs to its titled owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'either limit of land', meaning L or D, and written out that is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm carries this title, so it names a man of noble rank.

clue.text: Supervise foreign article being replaced by English

indicators.note: being replaced by means one letter swaps out for another

parts.note: oversea means abroad, foreign
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A foreign item is swapped for an English one under supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being replaced by' swaps the A (article) in OVERSEA for E (English).
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct work is to supervise it; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Note a benefit supplied by a sickness

parts.note: use means benefit, as in 'what's the use?'

explanation.surface: A doctor's note gives an advantage to someone off sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The queasy feeling of wanting to vomit is a kind of illness.

clue.text: Monarch is quite losing it, appearing almost rude

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

indicators.note: losing means having something taken away, so those letters come out

explanation.surface: A king grows quiet and almost offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing it' takes IT out of QUITE, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A risqué joke is slightly indecent, close to the edge of propriety without being outright vulgar.

clue.text: Marine creature expert gets a name after swimming etc.

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters first and the rest behind them
swimming letters float about and rearrange

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist in sea life gets a name after swimming, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' makes CET from 'etc.'; 'after' sets expert, a and name behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales, dolphins and porpoises belong to this order of mammals, all living in the sea.

clue.text: Disloyal feature raising a stink: party to be outlawed

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature

indicators.note: outlawed means banished, so these letters are thrown out

parts.note: something odorous gives off a smell
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A rebel's smelly habit gets a political party banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be outlawed' removes DO from ODOROUS, leaving OROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor betrays his country, so being treacherous like that is being disloyal.

clue.text: Son meeting father in spring

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A boy meets his dad in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural mineral spring, often a resort where people take the waters, is called by this name.

clue.text: Wood on the beach — no grey rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Driftwood on the shore, not grey rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun for the beach but is the verb shaking NOGREY into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden barrier built out from the shore to stop sand being washed away is called by this name.

clue.text: Right to protect Queen touring valley in response to emergency

indicators.note: to protect is to enclose for safety, so these letters go around the rest
touring means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: Royal bodyguards escort the Queen on a tour of the valley amid a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; 'touring' puts her around the valley, and 'to protect' puts Right's abbreviation around both.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest state of readiness is declared when danger threatens, so it is a reaction to a crisis.
